name: Cosmetics and beauty retail

problems.words: Best-selling shades go out of stock and we only notice when customers ask
quick_ideas: Pick out your top-selling shades, because those are the ones worth watching closely
Set a minimum quantity for each, because it gives staff a clear point to reorder.

workzap_build.text: shade-level stock with barcode scanning and a WhatsApp alert the moment a best seller drops below its minimum, across shop and online.

problems.ask_first: Roughly how many products and shades do you carry?
problems.free_stops: minimum levels and reorder rules are worked out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count empty spaces for your fastest moving shades at closing, so you see which shades are repeatedly missed before customers ask.
Give one staff member the shade check before lunch and closing, so reordering starts from shelf reality not assumptions.

problems.words: Products expire before we sell them
quick_ideas: Do one expiry sweep and move the earliest dates to the front, because new stock is often sold first
List what expires in the coming months, so you can bundle it in time without touching any dates.

workzap_build.text: batch and expiry tracking with near-expiry lists early enough to plan bundles or clearance.

problems.free_stops: alert timing and clearance planning are kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which products near expiry are still untouched after a full week on display, so slow lines stand out early.
Give one person the expiry shelf walk every Monday, so short dated stock gets noticed in time for normal selling.

problems.words: COD parcels get refused and the courier charges us both ways
quick_ideas: Confirm COD orders with the buyer before dispatch, because unconfirmed orders are the ones most often refused
List last month's refusals by area, because it shows where the problem sits.

workzap_build.text: every COD order confirmed automatically before dispatch, with each parcel tracked as confirmed, delivered or refused.

problems.ask_first: Is most of your online business COD?
problems.free_stops: the confirmation flow and its wording are kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note refused parcels by area and order source for one week, so you see where refusals are repeatedly starting.
Give one staff member the refused parcel notebook and courier handover, so every return is tracked the day it comes back.

problems.words: Courier COD money comes late and doesn't match
quick_ideas: Match one month of courier payments against your parcel list, because it shows exactly what's missing
Ask each courier for a parcel-wise statement, because totals hide gaps.

workzap_build.text: COD reconciliation showing dispatched, delivered, refused, remitted and outstanding per courier, updated daily.

problems.ask_first: How many couriers do you use?
problems.free_stops: the reconciliation setup per courier goes in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare each courier drop against the matching paid parcels in your order notebook, so delayed or short remittances surface quickly.
Keep one remittance list with one person updating it on payment days, so courier money stops getting checked from scattered notes.

problems.words: Instagram DMs are full of ‘price?' and ‘is this original?'
quick_ideas: Count a day's DMs and how many became orders, because it shows what the inbox is worth
Make one person responsible for replies, because shared inboxes get ignored.

workzap_build.text: one inbox for Instagram and WhatsApp where every chat is answered consistently and turned into a tracked order.

problems.free_stops: reply flows and catalogue links are kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many price messages become paid orders over one busy day, so you judge the real cost of reply time.
Assign one person each shift to clear selling messages, so order chats stop sinking under repeated product questions.

problems.words: We pay influencers and don't know what we got
quick_ideas: Give your next influencer their own code, because it's the simplest way to tie orders to them
List what each influencer was given, so you can compare later.

workzap_build.text: unique codes and links per influencer or campaign, with the orders each one brought in, reported automatically.

problems.ask_first: Do you pay influencers or send PR boxes, or both?
problems.free_stops: code setup and campaign reporting go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many order chats mention each influencer this week, so you see whose mentions actually bring buying conversations.
Keep one notebook page for influencer gifts and orders with one staff owner, so free stock is checked against sales talk.

problems.words: Website and shop stock never match, so we oversell
quick_ideas: Check your fastest items across every channel once, because it shows how far apart they've drifted
Make one person own stock numbers, because shared ownership means nobody updates.

workzap_build.text: one stock count shared by shop, website, Instagram and marketplaces like Daraz or Noon, with all orders in one pick-pack list.

problems.ask_first: Which marketplaces do you sell on?
problems.free_stops: channel connections and stock rules are kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare shelf count with the selling count kept elsewhere for your fastest items, so overselling risk shows before the next rush.
Make one person update stock after each sale block, so both shop and remote orders follow the same count.

problems.words: Customers complain we sent the wrong shade
quick_ideas: Store look-alike shades apart, because most mix-ups happen on the shelf
Check a day's packed orders before sealing, because it shows where errors creep in.

workzap_build.text: a pick-pack list with a barcode shade check and a packing photo saved against each order.

problems.free_stops: the packing check process goes in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which shades get corrected during packing over one week, so the look alike items causing complaints stand out.
Give one packer the final shade callout before sealing, so each parcel has a clear handover point for accuracy.

problems.words: Testers get used up or stolen, and small items walk out
quick_ideas: Count your testers and high-risk small items once, because you'll see the real loss
Move the most-taken items near the counter, because visibility deters.

workzap_build.text: a tester log and short daily spot-count on phone, with monthly cost written off by category and branch.

problems.ask_first: Where do you think most of the loss happens?
problems.free_stops: the count rotation and loss reporting are kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count testers and easy to pocket items at opening and closing, so loss by time of day becomes visible.
Give one counter staff member the tester and small item check, so shrinkage gets noticed from the same place daily.

problems.words: Customers buy once in a sale and never come back
quick_ideas: Start asking at billing if customers want restock news, saving numbers only with their permission
Note which products bring people back, because those are the ones to announce.

workzap_build.text: a consented customer list with WhatsApp messages for restocks and sales, and repeat buyers recognised.

problems.ask_first: Do you keep any record of who buys from you?
problems.free_stops: the messaging plan and loyalty rules go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Mark one week of sale bills against later walk in purchases, so you see which sale items fail to bring people back.
Keep one notebook at the counter for repeat buyer signs, so staff notice return visits without relying on memory.

problems.words: Staff give their own discounts to friends
quick_ideas: Review one month of discounts and voids by staff role, because patterns show quickly
Set clear discount limits by role, because grey areas invite misuse.

workzap_build.text: discount rules with caps, owner approval above limits and a weekly report by role.

problems.ask_first: Who can give discounts at the till now?
problems.free_stops: limits and approval routing are kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare staff discounts by shift against the same products sold full price, so friendly giveaways stop hiding inside busy hours.
Give one supervisor the discount notebook each day, so every reduction is tied to a visible check before billing.

never_say: Any advice on ingredients, product safety, allergies, skin conditions or what suits someone; for swelling or breathing difficulty, say seek emergency care.
Whether a product is genuine, or help selling "first copy" goods as originals.
Help to relabel, repack or change expiry dates.
Advice on import permits or cosmetic registration; say "check with your clearing agent or adviser".
Any promise that a campaign or influencer will bring sales.

sample_reply.person: Instagram pe orders bohat aate hain lekin COD ke aadhe parcel wapis aa jaate hain. Koi solution hai?
sample_reply.pi:
Bilkul, is ka hal mumkin hai, aur pehla qadam aasan hai.
Pehle, dispatch se pehle har COD order customer se confirm karwa lein, kyun ke bina confirmation wale parcel hi zyada wapis aate hain.
Doosra, pichle mahine ke wapis aaye parcels area ke hisaab se dekh lein, taake pata chale masla kahan hai.
Pakke hal ke liye Workzap ye banwa sakta hai: har COD order pe confirmation apne aap jaye aur har parcel ka status aur courier ki payment ek jagah nazar aaye.

Kya main aap ke liye solution document aur quote banwa doon? Mana bhi kar sakte hain.
